To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

reminding White US teens about Latino and (to a lesser extent) Asian/Asian-American celebrity exemplars increases their warmth toward the respective outgroup and, via that effect, increases their warmth toward other racial/ethnic outgroup members.

exposure to media-based information about US Latino and Asian/Asian American celebrities increased warmth toward those groups, and that these effects spilled over to affect judgments of other racial/ethnic and school-related groups.
reminders of Latino and Asian/Asian American celebrity exemplars positively affected White teens’ attitudes toward these groups and other groups, via warmth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of media in the socialization of adolescents’ intergroup attitudes.
the effects of media exposure to racial/ethnic exemplars on attitudes and judgments toward their respective groups, as well as toward other groups.
the effects of media exposure to famous exemplars of minority racial and ethnic groups on judgments about those groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of reminding White teens about Latino and AA celebrities are mostly positive.
the effects of reminding White teens about Latino and/or Asian American celebrities are mostly positive, and that these effects are largely mediated by warmth.
reminding White adolescents about Latino and Asian/Asian-American celebrity exemplars had mostly positive effects, and that these effects were mediated by warmth toward the groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reminders of positive outgroup exemplars may be a simple, effective way to promote positive intergroup relations.

the positive effect of reminding teens of Latino and Asian American celebrity exemplars on their warmth toward these groups is a robust effect that is not moderated by the racial stratification status of each group.
the positive effects of reminding teens about outgroup celebrities can be quite broad, but that they are not necessarily strong enough to overcome negative attitudes that have already developed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
media-based exposure to positive exemplars of outgroups can have positive effects, even for individuals with little prior experience with the group.
media-based exposure to famous exemplars of outgroups can increase positive attitudes about those outgroups, even among White adolescents.
media-based reminders of famous outgroup members can increase positive attitudes toward the group and, indirectly, increase positive attitudes toward other groups.
